body: I believe that [Issue #38373](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/38373) may also be related to this regression, which I guess could have been caused when [the cached dependencies in tests feature](https://indepth.dev/next-level-testing-in-angular-ivy-version-9/#faster-tests-with-ivy) was added.

Hi @smzelek,

Thanks for providing an example that illustrates the setup of the described use-case. This is indeed a known difference between View Engine and Ivy - in View Engine, components are compiled in the context of some environment - either a platform browser instance, or a test. Therefore each test must declare its own testing module and import what it wants to compile. In Ivy, there is only one compiled version of a component at any time, and this compilation happens independently of the TestBed. Therefore `TestBed.configureTestingModule` is not necessary if there are no changes being made to the component's "production" configuration.

Currently we are in a transition period where both View Engine and Ivy renderers exist in the codebase and are available to developers. In order to provide backwards compatibility for most common use-cases, we retained existing TestBed API semantics (which are designed around View Engine's behavior) and made it compatible with Ivy. Once View Engine is removed from the codebase, we plan to revisit the TestBed API and redesign it to better reflect Ivy semantics.

Thank you.

issue.body:
`tView` that is stored on a component def contains information about directives and pipes that are available in the scope of this component. Patching component scope causes `tView` to be updated. Prior to this commit, the `tView` information was not restored/reset in case component class is not declared in the `declarations` field while calling `TestBed.configureTestingModule`, thus causing `tView` to be reused between tests (thus preserving scopes information between tests). This commit updates TestBed logic to preserve `tView` value before applying scope changes and reset it back to the previous state between tests.

Closes #38600.

body:
Hi @smzelek,

Thanks for providing a new repro, the described scenario is not handled by Ivy TestBed and this is a bug. I performed additional investigation and found out that there is a piece of state that is preserved between tests in case a component is present in the `declarations` field while calling `TestBed.configureTestingModule` in one test, but it's absent (or the whole `TestBed.configureTestingModule` call is omitted) in the next test. I've created a PR that should address this issue, see https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/38659. Running tests from your repro with the changes from the mentioned PR make them pass/fail consistently independent of the order.

You can also test the behavior using an updated version of the `@angular/core` package using [this instruction](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/618cb32407196573e2e0e8a6763e7afdb2b52898/docs/DEVELOPER.md#getting-packages-from-build-artifacts) and [the core package from the mentioned PR](https://797947-24195339-gh.circle-artifacts.com/0/angular/core-pr38659-aef91ea13f.tgz).

Thank you.

issue.title: Ivy compatibility

repository.name: jest-preset-angular
repository.description: Jest configuration preset for Angular projects.

issue.body:
### Background

To turn TypeScript into JavaScript, Angular uses the TypeScript compiler, while also taking advantage of its own enhancements and processes. This practice was taken to the next level when the novel Ivy compiler was introduced, which optimizes the build even more and makes Angular a high-level web framework.

If tests running in jest just apply the TS-to-JS-compilation via `ts-jest` on the Angular code and try to run a tiny Angular App for a test case, many specialized scenarios miss the enhancements the Angular compiler does during Angular development.

The following identified scenarios are possibly such, although there are probably more:
* automatic recognition of `entryComponents` #353
* ngcc compilation issues #347
* running a test app without `ngZone` #354

To keep up with Ivy and further Angular enhancements, we want to depend more on the tools Angular provides.

PR #406 shows we are able to add Angular transformers in the preset.

### Basic Transformer Analysis

When looking for `TransformatorFactory` in the Angular codebase (July 2020), we find several transformers, such as
* [`inline_resources.ts`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/d1ea1f4c7f3358b730b0d94e65b00bc28cae279c/packages/compiler-cli/src/transformers/inline_resources.ts) A transformer to inline resources (such as `templateUrl` and `styleUrls`)
* [Source File TransformFactory](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/e648a0c4ca532a009186855c2ed998188fe0c9e3/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/shims/src/factory_generator.ts#L107-L124) **unclear** - *probably to keep track of which files are compiled*
* [Parens Wrapper](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce879fc4160e9b12db5d58fd20caf30fc05e8832/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/annotations/src/util.ts#L376-L386) Wraps content in parentheses
* [Constructor Parameters Downlevel Transformer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/66e6b932d818a161bd19c03e3e854a22552a7db2/packages/compiler-cli/src/tooling.ts) downlevels constructor parameters - for JIT compilation - we take advantage of this transformer in `jest-preset-angular` since #406
* [R3 Transformer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/d1ea1f4c7f3358b730b0d94e65b00bc28cae279c/packages/compiler-cli/src/transformers/r3_transform.ts) **unclear** - adds annotation for closure compiler
* [Alias Transformer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/d1ea1f4c7f3358b730b0d94e65b00bc28cae279c/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/transform/src/alias.ts) creates additional exports for exported aliases
* [Import Preserving Transformer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/d1ea1f4c7f3358b730b0d94e65b00bc28cae279c/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/imports/src/default.ts#L128-L134) prevents import declarations from being removed by the compiler
* [Declaration Transformer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/d1ea1f4c7f3358b730b0d94e65b00bc28cae279c/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/transform/src/declaration.ts#L68-L85) **unclear** handles `.d.ts` files
* [Ivy Transformer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/d1ea1f4c7f3358b730b0d94e65b00bc28cae279c/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/transform/src/transform.ts#L33-L44) applies changes from an IvyCompilation (incrementally?)


Further objects referenced as `transformers` are used in [`program.ts`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/66e6b932d818a161bd19c03e3e854a22552a7db2/packages/compiler-cli/src/transformers/program.ts)

-----

While we could just try to include all of them, it is a much better path to understand what we are doing and why.

Any help analyzing these and figuring out what these do does help a lot.
